label: RD-mrxs
description: External-validation set sourced from .mrxs whole-slide images. Found to carry systematically less apparent hematoxylin and a paler, washed-out appearance relative to the EBRAINS training distribution.
fitted_from_stageA: Stage-A thumbnails: 300 randomly sampled top-level {name}.jpg files under {subtype}/GS_batchrun_*/GS_*_hash/ (figures/ and *_Gunknown subtype folders excluded).
fitted_from_stageB: Stage-B patches: 300 randomly sampled figures/patch_rXcY.jpg files from the same run (stageA_riskmap.jpg and *_Gunknown subtype folders excluded).

validated_against.training_reference: 300 randomly sampled EBRAINS training thumbnails/patches (data/ebrains_thumbnails, data/stage_b_cohort_RN18_F1/patches)
validated_against.note: Radboud carries ~33% less apparent hematoxylin at Stage-A and ~39% less at Stage-B than the training reference. LAB lightness before/after normalization: Stage-A 88.7 -> 85.6 (target 79.7); Stage-B 77.8 -> 68.3 (target 67.6, near-exact). The a/b colour axes overshoot slightly past the target in both stages -- inspect normalized output visually before trusting blindly.

_note: stageA/stageB above are the shared class-balanced training target (same numbers as TCGA-Glioma.json's target -- there is only one target, fit once from training data; 'profile' selects WHETHER to correct and documents how that dataset compares to it, not a different target). UPDATED 2026-07-30 to the class-balanced version. This profile's own validated_against diagnostics below were computed via plain (non-stratified) uniform sampling of Radboud's pool and have NOT been recomputed with class stratification yet -- the Radboud data lives on an external drive (E:) that was not connected when this fix was made. Re-run the class-stratified characterization once it's available.
